# `kernel/execution/TwoPassPlannerFinalizer.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/execution/TwoPassPlannerFinalizer.js`

TwoPassPlannerFinalizer.js — the Phase 9 execution loop (kernel.aiExecutor). Full flow per OS.ai() task: prompt → goal classify → gather context (roots-checked resource reads, PrivacyGuard-scrubbed) → capability negotiation (Ph4/Ph5 attestation) → model-tier choice → PASS 1 planner (JSON plan; tools executed through the AI Tool Firewall with idempotency keys, policy gating and approval elicitations) → PASS 2 finalizer (strict schema, NO tools) → validator → repair-if-needed (bounded RepairLoop) → CommitCoordinator commit → Witness receipt → Task Ledger record. The pipeline is driven as Phase 6 storylets over worldState.phase; every fired storylet returns `{ pending }` (see AIStoryletFactory) which this loop awaits, then applies `{ phase, wsPatch, facts, observations }` via StoryletEffectsApplier.

### `parseSteeringModelClassification(value)`

Parse the advisory free-lane steering classifier. This envelope cannot grant authority, and `cancel` is intentionally absent so an uncertain model can never stop operator work. Prose/fences are tolerated only when they contain one bounded JSON object, which keeps small free models useful without making their formatting part of the task-control boundary.

### `validatePlannerTransportEnvelope(value)`

Validate the canonical OS planner envelope. Provider-side schema enforcement is never required: provider-native exact JSON is projected into this closed transport before local graph, descriptor, authority, and receipt validation. This validator remains the authoritative canonical boundary. The returned diagnostics contain schema paths only and never echo tool arguments or provider text.

### `validatePlannerTransportResponse(value)`

### `plannerResultTransportCandidate(result)`

Prefer a completed typed provider tool batch over assistant prose.

### `plannerTransportShapeEvidence(value)`

Return a content-free structural description of a planner response. Provider text is never copied. The evidence is safe for durable diagnostics and distinguishes common repair cases without guessing at model intent.

### `shouldContinueDodadAuthoringRepair({ attempt = 1, artifactKind = '', errorCode = '', reasonCodes = [], priorReasonCodes = [], } = {})`

Decide whether another clean-room authoring pass has new local evidence. Attempt one retains the existing general repair behavior. Later passes are admitted only for a newly observed local reason with an exact content-free repair directive owned by DodadForge. This avoids a hardcoded attempt ceiling while remaining finite for repeated model output and preserving fail-closed validation.

### `plannerTransportRejection(error, retainedText)`

Recover a locally repairable planner envelope from a terminal broker error. The kernel broker converts a rejected `resultValidator` verdict into a route failure and discards the provider result. When the selected route is pinned (manual routing) or every approved compatible route is exhausted, that error reaches the executor and would end the run — even though the exact rejected text is still available and repairable. Only malformed-kind local admission rejections with retained text qualify; policy, authority, abort, outage, and truncation failures stay terminal under their normal rules.

**Returns:** |null} recovery evidence, or null

### `normalizePlannerResponse(text)`

Normalize a planner response while accepting one safe prose outcome: an explicit statement that no tool calls are needed. This lets smaller local models finish a no-op planning round without inventing a tool invocation.

### `isDirectConversationPrompt(value)`

Bounded social turns should go straight to the answer pass. AI Echo advertises core tools on every turn, which must not force greetings, introductions, acknowledgements, or personal conversation through planner JSON. Explicit tool/OS action language always wins and stays on the planner.

Resolve the exact immutable source bound by Dodad Studio's tweak action. A generic mention of editing an artifact is deliberately insufficient: an update route needs the canonical artifact id, revision, and content hash so it cannot drift into broad filesystem discovery or create a replacement.

### `hasSavedArtifactWorkIntent(text)`

### `savedArtifactRequiredPlannerTools(text)`

### `savedArtifactPreferredKind(text)`

Resolve the saved-work storage kind requested by the operator. Web is the OS default because it preserves semantic structure, presentation, and optional interaction in either one self-contained document or an adaptive local graph. Every kind competes through the same weighted evidence scorecard.

### `selectDodadAuthoringShape(text, { kind = 'web', baseProject = null } = {})`

Select content shape independently from Artifact kind. Templates are hints; an existing verified graph wins for updates, while new ordinary web Dodads default to one complete document and expand only for explicit structural intent. Resource policy stays host-owned and never grants authority.

### `savedArtifactIntentProfile(text)`

Deterministic, content-local saved-work routing. Chat, web, document, code, table, chart, data, and declarative UI candidates all collect weighted positive, negative, and context signals. Explicit multi-word requests score strongly but never bypass comparison, ambiguity reporting, or negation. The scorecard is safe to expose in receipts and never grants tools, changes privacy classification, or replaces provider capability checks.

### `savedArtifactPlannerFormatContract(text)`

Content-free planner instruction for the exact default Artifact shape.

### `prioritizeRequiredPlannerTools(toolDescs, requiredNames = [])`

Present required tools first without changing the locally authoritative descriptor set. This is a provider-visibility projection only; it grants no capability and does not weaken descriptor or argument validation.

### `savedArtifactStoryletPlannerTools(storylet, state, mutationTarget)`

Restrict the generic planner to the one tool that can satisfy the active exact-update Storylet stage. Authoring, mutation, and revision verification are owned by the dedicated OS lane after a verified read, so they are never widened back into generic planner authority. `null` means this is not an exact saved-Artifact update lane. An empty array means the active update stage must not dispatch a generic planner tool.

### `bindSavedArtifactInspectPlan(plan, storylet, state, mutationTarget)`

Bind the inspect-current read to the complete immutable source revision. Provider-authored preview selectors such as `file` or `maxChars` cannot satisfy an exact update because the OS must preserve every unmentioned file. The user's revision-qualified mutation already authorizes this bounded read; this narrows the target and removes partial-read selectors before the task graph, approval, and tool-call signatures are compiled.

### `isTrustedWorkspaceRevisionPlannerDescriptor(tool)`

Recognize only the OS-owned, signed Workspace Faculty contracts. Names and tags are not authority: the planner projection must retain the exact implementation contract plus the live callable and signed package witness.

### `mountedVcsCommitStoryletPlannerTools(storylet, state, toolDescs = [])`

`null` means another Storylet; `[]` is a fail-closed missing capability.

### `taskStoryletPlannerTools(storylet, state, mutationTarget, toolDescs = [])`

Project the active declarative Storylet stage into a provider-visible tool allowlist. This is a restriction over already negotiated capabilities, not a capability grant. `null` keeps the negotiated set; `[]` is a local-only stage and therefore admits no generic planner action.

### `classifySavedArtifactPlanSteps(steps, pending = false, { preferredKind = '' } = {})`

Content-free obligation check used before executing a planner round.

### `buildSavedArtifactWebFiles({ title = 'AI Echo Artifact', authoredHtml = '' } = {})`

Build the deterministic three-file web project used by the OS-owned Artifact fallback. The authored HTML remains the model's work product while the shell, visual system, and progressive enhancement are local and stable.

### `savedArtifactFallbackTitle(text)`

Build a useful bounded title without trusting model-generated metadata.

### `normalizeSavedArtifactFallbackContent(value, { kind = 'document' } = {})`

Admit plain authored content before the OS constructs a signed mutation.

### `hasWorkspaceOutputLookupIntent(text)`

Detect a request to locate, verify, or explain the absence of saved output.

### `workspaceOutputSearchAssessment(toolResults)`

Project exact storage.search evidence into a bounded, content-free decision. A negative conclusion is complete only when VFS enumeration was untruncated and the same-task Workspace Output Index rebuild succeeded for /user.

### `isWorkspaceOutputMissingClaim(text)`

### `unattemptedObligationEvidence(obligation, toolDescription)`

Report a declared obligation that ended without a tool dispatch. The OS may only state what it observed. Recognizing refusal-shaped wording in planner prose is evidence that the round ended without an attempt, never evidence of *why*: the same words appear when a model merely discusses an earlier failure, and asserting a provider policy refusal from them puts a fabricated cause in front of the operator as OS evidence. The dispatch count is checkable, so that is what the finalizer is told.

### `isExplicitSavedArtifactRefusal(text)`

Recognize refusal-shaped planner prose tied to creating or saving a Dodad. This keeps that outcome off the JSON repair path, which cannot fix prose, while leaving arbitrary malformed planner output on the normal bounded repair path. It attests wording only — never a provider decision.

### `isExplicitSavedArtifactSuccessClaim(text)`

Recognize a claimed completed Artifact mutation, never execution evidence.

### `unfulfilledArtifactFinalClaimFailure(ws, answer)`

Reject a finalizer-discovered Artifact refusal before it can complete a generic action Storylet. This is intentionally a one-way safety boundary: provider prose may reveal that it recognized an exact Artifact target, but it can never establish successful execution. Only a verified Artifact mutation receipt can satisfy that action; command catalogs, status reads, and verification discovery remain support evidence.

### `unfulfilledArtifactRefusalFailure(ws, answer)`

Backward-compatible narrow projection used by refusal-specific callers.

### `currentUserPromptForRouting(value)`

AI Echo may wrap a short follow-up with bounded conversation history. Route on the explicit current-message section so old tool requests cannot turn a greeting or acknowledgement into a new planner round. The complete prompt remains untouched and is still supplied to the answer pass as context.

### `projectAITaskWorkflow(ws)`

Content-free workflow projection retained in FinalReport and Trajectory.

### `async projectAIContinuationDiagnostics(ws, outcome = 'failed')`

Durable content-free continuation provenance.  This semantic projection is independent of RunEventStream retention so a truncated trace still proves the exact request lineage, provider-visible tool surface, Storylet stage, and source/result Artifact relationship without retaining their values.

### `activeArtifactRoutingPrompt(ws)`

Resolve an OS-owned pending saved-work obligation without treating assistant prose or arbitrary older conversation as authority. The app binds this strict envelope only after selecting a still-pending durable action outcome.

### `livePatchRoutingText(value)`

Recover one narrow capability correction from AI Echo's managed follow-up wrapper without allowing arbitrary older turns to reactivate themselves.

### `normalizeFinalizerOutput(value, schema = DEFAULT_OUTPUT_SCHEMA, rawText = '')`

Normalize common provider answer envelopes without inventing answer content.

### `detectDeferredActionPromise(value)`

Detect a short terminal response that merely defers an OS action until after the run. The detector is deliberately narrow: it only admits first-person future/offer forms at the start of a short response and rejects no prose that already contains a result list, structured output, or an explicit failure.

### `isExplicitUserInputRequest(value)`

Recognize a real human-input boundary. A run may stop for an explicit choice, missing value, attachment, confirmation, or authorization; a bare future-action statement is not such a boundary.

### `unfulfilledActionClosureFailure(ws, kernel = null)`

Close action tasks against local execution evidence before asking a model to narrate the result. A failed or unstarted tool plan is not a completed task, and finalizer prose cannot turn it into one. Saved Dodads retain their stronger artifact-reference reconciliation contract below.

### `fileContentReadActionObligation(value)`

Recognize one explicit request to return a file's UTF-8 content.

### `readOnlyObservationSignature(results, toolDriver = null)`

Return a deterministic signature only when a round contains no mutation. Matching signatures mean both the calls and the resulting observations were unchanged, so another identical re-plan round cannot add evidence.

### `toolRoundSignature(results)`

A bounded deterministic fingerprint used to detect alternating planner cycles.

### `detectFinalToolEnvelope(answer, toolDriver = null, toolResults = [])`

Detect executable tool-call JSON leaked into final prose. A matching receipt proves the action ran, but it does not make a raw tool envelope a valid user answer. Fenced examples are ignored. The detector parses bounded complete objects and never evaluates model-authored content.

### `exactProviderUsageProjection(value)`

### `rebindDodadFailedRouteLineage({ priorCheckpointHash = '', rejectedCheckpointHash = '', priorRouteIds = [], rejectedRouteIds = [], } = {})`

### `proactiveToolCostCeiling(descriptor)`

These closed built-in operations invoke deterministic local/extension APIs. Generic commands, external workflows, media generation and model tools need a separate reviewed billing contract and remain proposals during autonomy.

### `providerUsageSample(result, phase, localTelemetry = null)`

### `aggregateProviderUsage(samples = [])`

### `resolveNegotiatedToolName(requestedName, capabilities = [])`

### `resolveNaviExecutionMode(kernel)`

### `plannerOutputParams(params)`

Guarantee the planner enough output budget to emit one complete action. Planner output is an exact, locally validated JSON envelope. Private model reasoning adds latency and consumes the same output allowance without advancing a task node, so it is explicitly disabled here. Raise the output floor only; a larger operator setting is always honoured.

### `adaptivePlannerOutputParams(params, context = {})`

Expand the planner's soft starting allowance when its compiled context is already large enough to make a 4K completion fragile. The provider still receives one legal request ceiling, but the app no longer freezes every Smart Routing plan at the generic 4K default. Explicit larger allowances are preserved, and provider compatibility preflight sees the expanded value.

### `dodadGranularAuthoringOutputParams(params, options = {})`

Size a surgical Dodad edit call from its exact localized source units. This is an adaptive starting allowance, never a creative output ceiling: an explicit larger route budget is preserved and broader neighborhoods grow the allowance without switching back to full-document drafting.

### `dodadAuthoringOutputParams(params, context = {})`

Reserve output space for a complete Dodad and adapt private reasoning effort from observed task state. A clean first pass starts at low effort; only a verified repair escalates to medium. Explicit operator effort and token budgets remain authoritative, so this layer never invents a hard ceiling.

### `jsonOnlyReasoningDirective(model)`

Return the model-native directive that suppresses a thinking trace, if the route documents one. NVIDIA Nemotron and hybrid Qwen3 were both trained on the same `/think` and `/no_think` soft switch, and both default to reasoning when no signal is present — which is why a JSON-only pass gets a monologue it never asked for. This is message text rather than an API parameter, so it needs no gateway support and a model that does not recognize it simply answers normally. The gateway alternatives do not cover every model family: OpenRouter can map caller-supplied `reasoning.max_tokens` or `effort` on compatible routes, but `exclude` still spends the budget on hidden thinking. Only JSON-only passes pass through here; prose answers keep their reasoning.

### `isTransientNaviExecutionState(value)`

### `naviCognitionDenialMessage(mode)`

Explain a cognition denial without hiding the exact kernel state or code. A still-transient state at the end of the startup budget is not the same condition as a terminal one: nothing is wrong with the operator's setup and the identical request usually succeeds once the bind settles. Saying only "unavailable" there sends operators looking for a fault that does not exist.

### `waitForNaviExecutionMode(kernel, { timeoutMs = NAVI_COGNITION_TRANSIENT_WAIT_MS, signal = null, } = {})`

Hold a newly accepted, still side-effect-free task across one short kernel authority rebind. The wait never bypasses Navi, never dispatches a provider, and resolves immediately when the state becomes ready or terminal.

### `resolveNaviFacultyToolInvocation(toolName, rawArgs = {})`

### `projectVerifiedFacultyOutcomeAck(receiptEvidence, replayed = false)`

Content-free learning projection from kernel-verified Faculty evidence. This carries no arguments, result payload, provider reasoning, capability, approval, or authority. Consumers may use it only as review evidence.

### `projectArtifactFileActivity({ toolName = '', args = {}, result = null, phase = 'preparing', errorCode = null, error = null, } = {})`

Project one local-only Artifact file operation for Run Details. A bounded incoming-content preview lets the operator inspect the exact write while it is active; it is never added to provider-visible results, signed receipts, diagnostics, or Companion messages. Exact absolute paths, sizes, and hashes still appear only after the locally verified Artifact receipt.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
